regions.label: Coracoid process
regions.description: A hook-shaped projection from the superior scapula, lying anterior to the glenoid and serving as an attachment for muscles and ligaments.

regions.label: Superior angle
regions.description: The superior angle is where the superior and medial borders of the scapula meet.

regions.label: Acromion
regions.description: The acromion continues laterally from the scapular spine and forms the bony roof above the shoulder joint.

regions.label: Clavicle
regions.description: An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.

regions.label: Intertubercular groove
regions.description: The groove between the greater and lesser humeral tubercles contains the tendon of the long head of biceps.

regions.label: Surgical neck
regions.description: The surgical neck is the narrowed region below the humeral tubercles, close to the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery.

regions.label: Lesser tubercle
regions.description: The lesser tubercle projects anteriorly from the proximal humerus and receives the subscapularis tendon.

regions.label: Greater tubercle
regions.description: The greater tubercle is the lateral prominence of the proximal humerus and receives supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor.

regions.label: Medial epicondyle
regions.description: The medial epicondyle projects from the distal humerus and gives origin to the common superficial flexor group.

regions.label: Lateral epicondyle
regions.description: The lateral epicondyle projects from the distal humerus and gives origin to the common extensor tendon.

regions.label: Trochlea
regions.description: The spool-shaped humeral trochlea articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna at the elbow.

regions.label: Coronoid process
regions.description: The coronoid process forms the anterior projection of the proximal ulna below the trochlear notch.

regions.label: Deltoid tuberosity
regions.description: The deltoid tuberosity is a rough lateral shaft prominence that receives the deltoid insertion.

regions.label: Humerus
regions.description: The long bone of the arm, articulating with the glenoid proximally and the radius and ulna distally; key landmarks include the surgical neck, radial groove and medial epicondyle.

regions.label: Ulna
regions.description: The medial forearm bone, whose olecranon and coronoid process form the trochlear notch around the humeral trochlea; its distal head is separated from the carpus by an articular disc.

regions.label: Ulna, styloid process
regions.description: The ulnar styloid process projects distally from the posteromedial aspect of the ulnar head.

regions.label: Radius, styloid process
regions.description: The radial styloid process projects distally from the lateral radius on the thumb side of the wrist.

regions.label: Carpal bones
regions.description: Eight short bones arranged in proximal and distal rows form the carpus between the forearm and metacarpals.

regions.label: Radius
regions.description: The lateral forearm bone in anatomical position, with a disc-shaped head proximally and a broad distal end that articulates with the scaphoid and lunate.

regions.label: Scapula
regions.description: A triangular flat bone on the posterolateral thoracic wall, spanning roughly ribs 2–7; its lateral angle bears the glenoid cavity and its spine expands into the acromion.

regions.label: Inferior angle
regions.description: The inferior angle is the meeting point of the medial and lateral scapular borders.

regions.label: Tuberosity of radius
regions.description: The radial tuberosity lies just distal to the radial neck and receives the biceps brachii tendon.

regions.label: Capitulum
regions.description: The rounded lateral articular surface of the distal humerus articulates with the head of the radius.

regions.label: Head of radius
regions.description: The disc-shaped radial head articulates with the capitulum and rotates within the annular ligament.

regions.label: C5 root of brachial plexus
regions.description: The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

regions.label: C6 root of brachial plexus
regions.description: The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.

regions.label: C7 root of brachial plexus
regions.description: The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.

regions.label: C8 root of brachial plexus
regions.description: The C8 ventral ramus ascends over the first rib to join T1 and form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

regions.label: T1 root of brachial plexus
regions.description: Most of the T1 ventral ramus joins C8 above the first rib to form the lower trunk; a smaller part remains as the first intercostal nerve.

regions.label: Dorsal scapular nerve
regions.description: A branch usually arising from the C5 root that pierces middle scalene and descends along the medial border of the scapula with the dorsal scapular artery.

regions.label: Upper trunk of brachial plexus
regions.description: The union of the C5 and C6 ventral rami at the lateral border of the scalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions above the clavicle.

regions.label: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
regions.description: The continuation of the C7 ventral ramus through the interscalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions behind the clavicle.

regions.label: Lower trunk of brachial plexus
regions.description: The union of C8 and T1 ventral rami, lying inferiorly in the plexus before dividing behind the clavicle.

regions.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
regions.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

regions.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
regions.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

regions.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
regions.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

regions.label: Suprascapular nerve
regions.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

regions.label: Lateral pectoral nerve
regions.description: A branch of the lateral cord that crosses anterior to the axillary artery, pierces clavipectoral fascia and chiefly supplies pectoralis major.

regions.label: Medial pectoral nerve
regions.description: A branch of the medial cord that typically pierces pectoralis minor and continues into the deep surface of pectoralis major.

regions.label: Axillary artery
regions.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

regions.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
regions.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

regions.label: Axillary nerve
regions.description: A C5–C6 terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery and winds around the surgical neck.

regions.label: Median nerve
regions.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

regions.label: Radial nerve
regions.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

regions.label: Ulnar nerve
regions.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

regions.label: Thoracodorsal nerve
regions.description: A posterior-cord branch that descends along the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal vessels to reach latissimus dorsi.

regions.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
regions.description: A small medial-cord branch that descends along the medial axillary and brachial vessels to supply skin of the medial arm.

regions.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm
regions.description: A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

regions.label: Long thoracic nerve
regions.description: The long thoracic nerve arises from C5-C7 roots and descends superficially on serratus anterior along the lateral thoracic wall.

regions.description: A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

regions.label: Coracobrachialis
regions.description: Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

regions.label: Pectoralis major
regions.description: Pectoralis major converges from the clavicle and anterior chest wall to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.

regions.label: Serratus anterior
regions.description: Serratus anterior attaches the lateral thoracic wall to the anterior surface of the medial scapular border.

regions.label: Supraspinatus
regions.description: A rotator-cuff muscle arising in the supraspinous fossa, passing beneath the acromion and inserting on the superior facet of the greater tubercle.

regions.label: Subscapularis
regions.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle filling the subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

regions.label: Teres major
regions.description: Teres major passes from the inferior scapula to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus and contributes to the posterior axillary fold.

regions.label: Coraco-acromial ligament
regions.description: A strong triangular band from the coracoid process to the acromion that forms the roof of the coracoacromial arch above the humeral head.

regions.label: Pectoralis minor
regions.description: Pectoralis minor passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process and forms part of the anterior wall of the axilla.

regions.label: Subclavius
regions.description: Subclavius lies below the clavicle and runs from the first rib and its costal cartilage to the inferior clavicular surface.

regions.label: Clavicle
regions.description: An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.

regions.label: Levator scapulae
regions.description: Levator scapulae descends from upper cervical transverse processes to the upper medial border of the scapula.

regions.label: Infraspinatus
regions.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle occupying the infraspinous fossa and inserting on the middle facet of the greater tubercle.

regions.label: Teres minor
regions.description: A narrow rotator-cuff muscle along the lateral scapular border that inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle.

regions.label: Latissimus dorsi
regions.description: Latissimus dorsi passes from the back to the floor of the humeral intertubercular sulcus and forms part of the posterior axillary fold.

regions.label: Trapezius
regions.description: Trapezius attaches to the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and helps position and rotate the scapula.

regions.label: Metatarsals

regions.label: Great cardiac vein
regions.description: The great cardiac vein ascends in the anterior interventricular groove and then follows the left atrioventricular groove toward the coronary sinus.

regions.label: Circumflex artery
regions.description: The circumflex branch of the left coronary artery follows the left part of the atrioventricular groove toward the posterior surface of the heart.

regions.label: Coronary sinus
regions.description: The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.

regions.label: Apex of heart
regions.description: The left ventricle forms the apex of the heart, which points inferiorly, anteriorly and to the left.

regions.label: Middle cardiac vein
regions.description: The middle cardiac vein follows the inferior interventricular groove and drains into the coronary sinus near its right atrial opening.

regions.label: Inferior interventricular artery
regions.description: This artery descends in the inferior, traditionally posterior, interventricular groove. The illustrated arrangement shows it arising from the right coronary artery.

regions.label: Small cardiac vein
regions.description: The small cardiac vein accompanies the right coronary vessels and joins the coronary sinus on the posterior aspect of the heart.

regions.label: Right coronary artery
regions.description: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and follows the right atrioventricular groove.

regions.label: Right atrium
regions.description: The right atrium receives the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus and opens into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

regions.label: Inferior vena cava
regions.description: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm and enters the inferior aspect of the right atrium.

regions.label: Pulmonary valve
regions.description: The pulmonary valve guards the outflow of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk and has three semilunar leaflets.

regions.label: Aortic valve
regions.description: The aortic valve guards the outlet from the left ventricle into the aorta and consists of three semilunar leaflets.

regions.label: Left coronary artery
regions.description: The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus and passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle before dividing into its principal branches.

regions.label: Right coronary artery
regions.description: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and follows the right atrioventricular groove.

regions.label: Atrioventricular bundle
regions.description: The atrioventricular bundle traverses the fibrous cardiac skeleton and continues into the ventricular conduction system.

regions.label: Coronary sinus
regions.description: The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.

regions.label: Middle cardiac vein
regions.description: The middle cardiac vein follows the inferior interventricular groove and drains into the coronary sinus near its right atrial opening.

regions.label: Inferior interventricular artery
regions.description: This artery descends in the inferior, traditionally posterior, interventricular groove. The illustrated arrangement shows it arising from the right coronary artery.
